mark_split.label: Name the angles and find their other ratios

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.72 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 74.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 16. The opening question of the chapter and the one that sets its habit: an inverse trig value is NOT something to evaluate — it is named as an angle, and the ordinary compound-angle formulas then do all the work. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. NOTE: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot, and this book has no Inverse Trig LAQ chapter (LAQ chapters are 1-6) and no VSAQ chapter (VSAQ chapters are 14-19). The same shape as Unit 7. Verified by walking to p.75, where SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles begins.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Name the angles and find their other ratios
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Call each inverse an angle, then get the missing ratio from sin²+cos²=1. The fast exam route is to sketch the right triangle: sinα = 4/5 means opposite 4, hypotenuse 5, so the third side is 3 and cosα = 3/5.
lines: Take Sin⁻¹(4/5) = α and Sin⁻¹(7/25) = β
Required To Prove (RTP): α + β = Sin⁻¹(117/125),

recall.must_convey: That each inverse is named as an angle and its other ratio found — sinα = 4/5 gives cosα = 3/5, and sinβ = 7/25 gives cosβ = 24/25.
accept: name each inverse as an angle then find the cosine from the sine using the right triangle
let sin inverse four fifths be alpha so sin alpha is four fifths and cos alpha is three fifths
take them as alpha and beta and get the other ratios
prathi inverse ni angle ga peru petti, migatha ratio kanukovali
convert the inverses into angles and find their cosines

steps.why: An inverse trig value cannot be added directly, but ANGLES can. Naming them turns the whole question into ordinary trigonometry.
common_mistakes: Trying to add the fractions 4/5 and 7/25 directly.
Forgetting to restate what has to be proved in terms of sin(α+β).

steps.label: Apply the sin(A+B) formula
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Both angles are given by their SINES, and the target is a Sin⁻¹ — so the sine addition formula is the right one to reach for.
lines: sin(α + β) = sinα cosβ + cosα sinβ

recall.must_convey: That sin(α+β) = sinα cosβ + cosα sinβ is applied, giving 117/125.
accept: use sin A plus B equals sin A cos B plus cos A sin B to get one seventeen over one twenty five
ninety six over one twenty five plus twenty one over one twenty five is one seventeen over one twenty five
sin alpha cos beta plus cos alpha sin beta apply cheyyali
the sine of the sum is one seventeen by one twenty five

steps.why: The target tells you which formula to use. A Sin⁻¹ on the right means the sine of the sum is what must be computed.
common_mistakes: Using cos(A+B) and computing the wrong thing.
Multiplying the wrong pairs — it is sinα with cosβ, not sinα with sinβ.

steps.label: Convert back to an inverse
steps.margin_note: Last mark. sin(α+β) = 117/125 means α+β is the angle whose sine is 117/125 — which is exactly Sin⁻¹(117/125). Write that line; the computation alone is not the proof.

recall.must_convey: That sin(α+β) = 117/125 is converted back to α + β = Sin⁻¹(117/125), and the original statement restated.
accept: since the sine of the sum is one seventeen over one twenty five the sum is sin inverse of that
convert back to the inverse form to finish
alpha plus beta equals sin inverse one seventeen by one twenty five
sine value nunchi inverse ki malli marchali
write the result back in inverse form
heard_as: one seventeen over one twenty five

steps.why: The question was asked in inverse notation, so the answer must return to it. Stopping at a fraction answers a different question.
common_mistakes: Ending at sin(α+β) = 117/125 without converting back.
Writing the answer as a decimal.
